family.name: LX & GX
family.verdict: Land Cruisers that went to finishing school and somehow kept their boots on. The badge says country club; the frame rails say Gobi Desert.
intro: Lexus got into the off-road business the way a rich kid gets into punk rock: by borrowing a band that was already good. The first LX 450, which reached US buyers as a 1996 model, was almost entirely the J80 Land Cruiser with leather, wood and a new grille. Every LX since has been built on the Land Cruiser of its day, from the 100 Series-based LX 470 through the 200 Series-based LX 570 to today's 300 Series-based LX 600.

The GX arrived for 2003 as the smaller sibling, built on the J120 Land Cruiser Prado that the rest of the world got and North America didn't. It was followed by the Prado 150-based GX 460 for 2010 and, for 2024, the GX 550, which shares the GA-F platform with the J250 Land Cruiser 250 / Prado.

For the hands-on crowd the appeal is simple: Toyota's ladder frames, low-range transfer cases and famously long-lived engines, sold new to people who mostly never left the pavement. That means plenty of well-maintained, lightly abused trucks on the used market, along with the expensive suspension gadgets that luxury brought with them.

generations.name: LX 450
generations.summary: The first Lexus truck, a lightly disguised 80 Series Land Cruiser with a 212-hp 4.5-liter straight-six. Sold for two US model years only.

generations.name: LX 470
generations.summary: 100 Series Land Cruiser underneath, with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and hydraulic Adjustable Height Control (AHC) suspension.

generations.name: LX 570
generations.summary: The 200 Series twin, powered by the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE V8 (383 hp in US/Canada trim).

generations.name: LX 600
generations.summary: Unveiled in October 2021 on the 300 Series platform. Swaps the V8 for a 409-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.

generations.name: GX 470
generations.summary: Prado 120 underneath, with the 2UZ-FE V8 and a full-time 4WD system that has a locking center diff. Today it's one of the best-value overland platforms money can buy.

generations.name: GX 460
generations.summary: Prado 150-based, with a 301-hp 4.6-liter V8, six-speed automatic and Torsen center locking differential. It famously earned (and lost) a Consumer Reports 'Don't Buy' in 2010.

generations.name: GX 550
generations.summary: Boxy again, and proud of it. It shares the GA-F platform with the Land Cruiser 250 and uses a 349-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.

page.title: Lexus GX 470
page.verdict: A Prado in a dinner jacket with a V8 that refuses to die. The trick is buying one before the previous owner's deferred maintenance becomes yours.

paragraphs: The Lexus GX 470 is a Land Cruiser Prado 120, the mid-size Land Cruiser the rest of the world got and North America never did, dressed for a suburb it was always overqualified for. Underneath the wood trim are a ladder frame, a four-link solid rear axle with a lateral rod, full-time four-wheel drive with low range and a lockable center differential, plus Toyota's 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8. It was sold to people who wanted a nice SUV. It is now bought by people who want to cross Nevada on dirt roads.

story.heading: A PRADO FOR AMERICA
paragraphs: Development started in 1999, two years after the J120 Prado program it was built on, and design work was finished in the first half of 2000. Lexus showed the GX at the 2002 North American International Auto Show as a 2003 model, and sales began in November 2002. It was slotted underneath the [[lexus/lx470|LX 470]], which was itself a [[land-cruiser/100-series|100 Series]] Land Cruiser in a suit.

The GX had company on the Tahara assembly line. Expedition Portal notes it was built on the same line as the Prado and the [[4runner/4th-gen|4th-gen 4Runner]], and the 4Runner shares its suspension layout, rear air springs included on some trims. That family resemblance is useful. Forum regulars routinely borrow 4Runner parts, tire-fitment data and even used steering racks for their GXs.

story.heading: THE 2UZ AND THE GADGETS
paragraphs: At launch the 2UZ-FE made 235 hp and 320 lb-ft. Variable valve timing (VVT-i) arrived for 2005 and pushed output to 270 hp. A change in SAE testing procedures restated that as 263 hp from 2006, with no actual change to the hardware. Midway through 2004, a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch raised the tow rating from 5,000 to 6,500 lb. The transmission also became a sealed unit with no dipstick that year.

Lexus being Lexus, the clever hardware came with complications. The rear axle rides on air springs with ride-height control, and the dampers are driver-adjustable through Adaptive Variable Suspension. Downhill Assist Control handles steep descents, and KDSS, a hydraulically linked anti-roll system, became an option late in the 2004 model year. All of it works brilliantly until it gets old. Then the air springs leak, the compressor wears itself out chasing them, and the truck sits on its bump stops.

story.heading: WHY OVERLANDERS LOVE IT
paragraphs: Four Wheeler magazine named the GX its Four Wheeler of the Year for 2003 and 2004, which was unusual praise for a vehicle with a Mark Levinson stereo option. Expedition Portal's project truck called the J120 "often considered the pinnacle of the body-on-frame era" and called the V8 "one of the most reliable engines ever sold in the USA." It also pointed to a 109-inch wheelbase and payload higher than the 4Runner's.

The weak points are well mapped. Owners report aging steering racks, CV boots, lower ball joints and cracked exhaust manifolds (often the driver's side), plus the timing belt that someone eventually has to pay for. Lexus ran a warranty enhancement program for cracked or sticky dashboards on 2003–2008 trucks. None of these problems scares off people who own a floor jack, which is why aftermarket support is now deep: lifts, rear coil conversions, skids, sliders and bumpers built specifically for this truck.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: US sales peaked at 35,420 in 2004 and slid to 6,235 in 2009. A 2008 facelift brought a dark metallic grille, graphite-finish wheels and more chrome. The [[lexus/gx460|GX 460]] replaced it after debuting in November 2009, followed by the boxy [[lexus/gx550|GX 550]], which shares its bones with the [[land-cruiser/250-series|250 Series]] Land Cruiser.

The GX 470's afterlife has been kinder than its retirement. Cheap examples with high mileage and full service records are the starter overland rig of choice, because the V8 lasts and the chassis was always a Land Cruiser. The suspension complexity is optional. You can retire it with a coil conversion and a Saturday afternoon.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE PROJECT TRUCK
callout.title: Expedition Portal's GX 470 build
paragraphs: When Expedition Portal turned a GX 470 into a project vehicle, it kept the factory rear airbags for load leveling, added a 60 mm Air Lift 52420 spacer and fitted Old Man Emu BP-51 shocks. It rebuilt the steering rack, replaced the CV axles with factory Toyota parts and added Timbren bump stops, an ARB Summit bar, a Warn Zeon 10-S winch and 255/80R17 Toyo A/T III tires, which measured just over 33 inches.

Two lessons from that build are worth noting. First, an airbag failure left the truck unable to be driven out, and it needed a tow. Second, an editor's note pointed out that ARB doesn't list the GX as an approved application for its products, so fitting ARB parts to a GX may void ARB's warranty.

page.engineering_intro: The GX 470 is a J120 Prado underneath: a high-strength ladder frame, coil-over independent front suspension and a four-link solid rear axle with a lateral rod. Full-time 4WD runs through a two-speed transfer case and a helical limited-slip center differential that can be locked, with open differentials front and rear and brake-based A-TRAC traction control to cover for them. Lexus then layered on rear air springs with height control, adjustable dampers and, as an option from 2004, KDSS.

engineering.note: Shared with the Land Cruiser Prado 120. The 4th-gen 4Runner shares its suspension layout.
32-valve quad-cam with a timing belt. VVT-i from 2005.
Two-speed transfer case and a lockable helical LSD center diff. VSC switches off when the center diff is locked.
Owners call the factory spring rate soft. Optional KDSS adds a hydraulically linked anti-roll system.
Lexus calls it a 4-link (plus a lateral rod). Air springs with height control. Many owners convert to coils.
Brake-based traction control plus Downhill Assist Control. There are no factory axle lockers.

generations_table.note: Launch year. Rated to tow 5,000 lb.
Added curtain airbags, TPMS and a sealed transmission. A mid-year hitch upgrade raised towing to 6,500 lb, and KDSS became optional late in the year.
VVT-i and ULEV II certification. New Sport model.
Same engine, restated under revised SAE testing.
Facelift with a dark grille, graphite wheels and more chrome.

buying_checks.head: Frame rust
buying_checks.body: Forum veterans call this the biggest concern on trucks from the salt belt. Get underneath with a light and a screwdriver, or ask for close-up photos of the frame. Rust on the rear air-spring perches is also what kills the airbags.

buying_checks.head: Rear air suspension
buying_checks.body: Look for a rear end that sags overnight, a blinking height-control light, a harsh ride or a compressor that runs constantly. Spray soapy water where each airbag folds over its lower perch. If the system is already converted to coils, ask whose kit was used.

buying_checks.head: Timing belt history
buying_checks.body: The 2UZ-FE uses a belt that Toyota schedules at 90,000 miles, and the water pump runs off it. If there's no receipt, budget roughly $1K at a shop or a weekend of your own time. Engine Builder classes all belt-driven Toyota V8s as interference engines, so don't gamble on an unknown belt.

buying_checks.head: Cold-start tick
buying_checks.body: A tick that fades as the engine warms is the classic sign of a cracked exhaust manifold, often on the driver's side. The repair is a big one, so treat it as a price negotiation point.

buying_checks.head: Steering rack
buying_checks.body: Look for wet rack boots and power-steering fluid on the crossmember, and listen for creaking or whining at full lock. One ClubLexus owner's rack began creaking and whining loudly at about 130k miles.

buying_checks.head: Front end wear
buying_checks.body: Check for torn lower ball-joint boots and grease slung from the CV boots, and listen for clunks over bumps. Many trucks need lower control arms or ball joints, CV axles and front bearings at this age.

buying_checks.head: KDSS or not?
buying_checks.body: Turn the key and watch for a momentary KDSS light, or look for the oversized front sway bar. KDSS improves stability and articulation, but some skids and sliders need KDSS-specific versions or modifications.

buying_checks.head: Dashboard
buying_checks.body: Heat cracks and sticky dashboard surfaces are common enough that Lexus ran a warranty enhancement program for 2003–2008 GX 470s. Check whether the dash was already replaced, and confirm with a dealer whether any coverage still applies.

repairs.title: Rear air spring replacement or coil conversion
repairs.time: ≈ 2 hours (simple coil swap) to half a day (with new trailing arms)
repairs.cost: Under $200 in parts for a basic coil swap (owner report)
repairs.symptoms: The rear sits low or sags overnight, the ride turns harsh, the height-control light blinks, the compressor runs nonstop, and in the worst case the truck is sitting on its bump stops.
repairs.fix: First confirm the leak with soapy water where each bag folds over its perch. To keep air, replace both springs, and the compressor if it has worn out chasing leaks. To convert, support the axle, remove the shocks, cut the air lines and pop each bag's upper U-clip with a flat-head screwdriver, then fit a coil conversion kit with springs, retainers and isolators. The ride-height sensor sits on the upper trailing arm, and the compressor and reservoir live on the driver's side. Recheck bolt torque after 100 miles.
repairs.tools: Floor jack · jack stands · flat-head screwdriver · line cutters · torque wrench · coil conversion kit (e.g. Metal Tech 4x4 hardware with Icon 52800 3-in coils) · or Arnott air springs and compressor (P-3192) to stay on air

parts.name: OME MT64 2–3 in suspension lift, GX 470 (coil rear)

repairs.title: Timing belt and water pump
repairs.time: ≈ a full weekend for a first-timer
repairs.cost: About $950–$1,770 at shops, as quoted by owners on ClubLexus (the higher figure included a radiator and plugs)
repairs.symptoms: No symptoms until it fails, which is the problem. Due every 90,000 miles. The water pump is belt-driven, so a weeping pump or coolant crust behind the timing covers is a good reason to do both now.
repairs.fix: Remove the fan and shroud, accessory belts and crank pulley, then the timing covers. Set the engine to its timing marks and replace the belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump, plus the thermostat and hoses while you're in there. Before installing the new belt, compare its tooth count and alignment marks against the old one, because Engine Builder warns that even a half-tooth error means doing the job twice. Watch for P0011, P0016, P0018 or P0021 afterward, which can point to timing misalignment.
repairs.tools: Crank pulley holder · long breaker bar · torque wrench · coolant · belt kit with tensioner, idlers and water pump (OEM or Aisin-type kit)

parts.name: Aisin timing belt kit with water pump and tensioner, LX 470/GX 470 (TKT-021)
Thermostat, 2UZ-FE (90916-03100, the OEM number GXOR lists)
Coolant (use Toyota Super Long Life or equivalent), 2005 GX 470

repairs.title: Exhaust manifold replacement (often the driver's side)
repairs.time: Same-day job at a specialist shop
repairs.cost: Parts plus labor (high: engine mounts have to come out)
repairs.symptoms: A ticking noise from the engine bay that is loudest cold and often fades as the manifold heats and expands. The cause is a paper-thin crack where the flange meets the first pipe.
repairs.fix: Soak every fastener in penetrating oil for days beforehand. The engine mounts must be released, and the engine raised, to reach the lower manifold studs. Replace the manifold assembly with new gaskets, studs and nuts. Expect seized or broken studs on rusty trucks. Afterward, idle the engine for about half an hour to burn off manufacturing oil.
repairs.tools: Engine support or jack · penetrating oil · stud extractor set · new manifold, gaskets, studs and nuts

parts.name: Exhaust flange studs and nuts, 2005 GX 470
Exhaust manifold gasket, 2UZ-FE to 04/2005 (confirm for VVT-i trucks)

repairs.title: Steering rack replacement
repairs.time: ≈ half a day plus an alignment
repairs.cost: $1,900 at an independent shop including tie-rod ends and high-pressure hoses (owner report). Parts run from about $300 for an aftermarket rack to about $1,000 for new OEM.
repairs.symptoms: Wet rack boots, a falling power-steering reservoir, and creaking or whining on every turn of the wheel.
repairs.fix: First confirm the source: clean the engine bay and recheck, because hoses and the pump can drip onto the rack. Then disconnect the tie-rod ends and pressure lines, unbolt the rack and swap in an OEM reman unit with new bushings. While it's out, remove and clean the reservoir and its mesh screen, and consider an inline filter. Bleed the system, then get an alignment.
repairs.tools: Tie-rod end puller · flare-nut wrenches · drain pan · ATF/PS fluid · OEM reman rack (e.g. CVJ or Cardone) · new rack bushings

parts.name: Steering rack end (inner tie rod), GX 470
Power steering fluid (Dexron II/III type), 2005 GX 470

repairs.title: Front lower ball joints and control arms
repairs.time: ≈ half a day for both sides
repairs.cost: About $270 per OEM lower control arm (owner report, 4Runner V8 part). The OEM ball joint is only sold with the arm.
repairs.symptoms: Torn ball-joint boots weeping grease, clunks over bumps, and vague steering. Worn lower control arm bushings add knocks of their own.
repairs.fix: Either replace the whole lower control arm with its new ball joint and bushings, or press out the old joint and press in an aftermarket one (owners cite MOOG K500017 and Sankei 555). Make sure the grease fitting faces an accessible direction, and grease the new joint if it shipped dry. Buy KDSS or non-KDSS parts to match your truck, then align it.
repairs.tools: Ball-joint press · pickle fork or joint separator · torque wrench · grease gun · lower control arm or ball joint

parts.name: SuperPro front lower control arm set, GX 470 non-KDSS

repairs.title: Front CV axle replacement
repairs.symptoms: Grease slung around the inside of the wheel, split CV boots, and clicking on tight turns.
repairs.fix: Loosen the axle nut with the wheel on the ground, then lift the truck. Separate the lower ball joint or tie rod enough to swing the knuckle, pull the axle out of the hub and pop the inner joint from the differential. Install a new axle; Expedition Portal's project truck used factory Toyota parts. Torque the axle nut, then stake or pin it.
repairs.tools: Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · pry bar · joint separator · torque wrench · new axle nut and OEM axle

parts.name: CV boot kit, OEM Toyota, GX 470/150 Series

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The stock size is 265/65R17. On a stock or nearly stock GX 470, the safe consensus is about 31.5 inches. Owners report 265/70R17 working with little or no rubbing (one reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse), and 255/75R17 with zero rubbing. Going to 33 inches (285/70R17, or the narrower 255/80R17) generally means a 2–3 in lift and some liner trimming.

faq.q: How much can a GX 470 tow?
faq.a: 2003 models are rated for 5,000 lb. Midway through the 2004 model year, Lexus fitted a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch and raised the rating to 6,500 lb.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: The EPA rates it at 14 mpg city, 18 highway and 15 combined (2007), and it calls for premium fuel. Bigger tires typically cost owners another 1 to 1.5 mpg.

faq.q: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
faq.a: It's a belt. Toyota's interval for UZ V8s is 90,000 miles, and the belt drives the water pump, so most owners replace both together.

faq.q: What fluids and capacities does it take?
faq.a: Per the 2005 factory repair manual: engine oil 5W-30, 6.5 US qt (6.2 L) with filter. The A750F automatic takes Toyota Genuine ATF WS only, about 3.2 qt (3.0 L) per drain-and-fill and 11.0 qt (10.4 L) dry. Transfer case: 1.5 qt (1.4 L, about 3 pints) of GL-5 75W-90. Front diff 1.48 qt (1.40 L) and rear diff 3.22 qt (3.05 L), both GL-5 SAE 90 (80W-90 below 0°F). Coolant is about 13.6 qt (12.9 L) of Toyota Super Long Life. Confirm against your own manual for your model year.

faq.q: When should I lock the center diff?
faq.a: Lock it whenever you're off pavement with loose traction. Many owners leave it locked for all trail driving, because it cuts down how much A-TRAC has to work on climbs. Unlock it for very tight turns on grippy surfaces and back on pavement. VSC is disabled while the center diff is locked.

faq.q: Should I keep the rear air suspension?
faq.a: It works well while healthy, and Expedition Portal's build kept it for load leveling. But aging bags leak where they fold over rusty perches, compressors wear out chasing those leaks, and a failure can leave you on the bump stops. Many owners convert to coils for well under the cost of new air parts.

faq.q: How do I tell if a GX 470 has KDSS?
faq.a: Watch for a momentary KDSS light when you turn the key, or look for the noticeably large front sway bar. It was optional from late in the 2004 model year. It helps both stability and articulation, but it complicates some armor installs.

2005 and later get the VVT-i engine (rated 270 hp, then restated as 263 hp from 2006). Trucks from mid-2004 on get the 6,500 lb hitch. 2008–2009 trucks have the facelift. In practice, condition beats model year: rust, timing-belt records, air suspension, steering rack and manifold matter more than the build date.

Common choices are Icon's 0–3.5 in systems (sold by Metal Tech 4x4), ToyTec kits, and Old Man Emu BP-51 coilovers, which Expedition Portal used. ARB doesn't list the GX as an approved application, so check warranty terms first. Pair any front lift with a rear coil conversion or an air spacer to level it.

Not quite. It's a Land Cruiser Prado 120 underneath. The 4th-gen 4Runner shares its suspension layout and was built on the same Tahara line, so many parts and much of the forum knowledge carry across. The GX had the V8 and full-time 4WD with a center lock as standard.

mods.why: The factory front springs are soft, and a 2–3 in lift is the usual step up to 33-in tires.

mods.cat: REAR AIR: COIL CONVERSION OR REPAIR
mods.why: This retires the aging air bags and compressor for good, or replaces them if you want to keep the self-leveling.
The factory underbody protection is thin, and the oil pan, transfer case and fuel tank sit right in the line of fire.
The factory running boards are about 30 lb of rock magnet. Real sliders protect the rockers and still work as a step. Get KDSS-specific instructions if your truck has it.
Low-profile bumpers improve approach angle, and a swing-out rear carrier gets a full-size spare out from under the truck.
At this age, racks, lower control arms and CV axles are wear items. OEM reman parts are the forum favorite over cheap new aftermarket.
A winch on a proper bumper, plus a jack that can still lift a lifted truck on big tires.

baseline_service.intro: Most GX 470s are well past the 90,000-mile timing-belt interval, so a used one should be treated as overdue until you see a receipt. Baseline every fluid as well. The 2005 factory repair manual (posted on GXOR) gives the specs below, and GXOR flags two GX-specific checks: the 2003–05 front differential support and the rear air springs.

items.spec: SAE 5W-30 multigrade (5W-30 is the manual's best choice) · 6.5 US qt (6.2 L) with filter
items.interval: At purchase, then every 5,000 mi / 6 months (2008 Lexus schedule)
items.note: Spin-on filter. Replace the drain-plug gasket every time.

items.spec: Belt, water pump, tensioner and idlers. GXOR's parts list adds a fan pulley bracket, radiator hoses, drive belt, thermostat and radiator cap.
items.note: If there's no receipt, assume it's due. Use about two gallons of Toyota Super Long Life pink premix for the refill (GXOR).

parts.name: Aisin timing belt kit with water pump (TKT-021)

items.spec: Toyota Super Long Life coolant or equivalent · 13.6 US qt (12.9 L)
items.interval: First at 100,000 mi / 120 months, then every 50,000 mi / 60 months
items.note: Usually done alongside the timing belt and water pump.

items.spec: Denso SK20R11 or NGK IFR6A11 · gap 1.0–1.1 mm
items.note: Replace the spark-plug tube seals if the valve covers come off.

items.interval: Replace every 30,000 mi. Inspect more often on dusty roads.
items.note: If the filter is oily, the factory manual says the PCV valve may be stuck.

items.spec: Toyota Genuine ATF WS only · 3.2 US qt (3.0 L) per drain-and-refill, 11.0 US qt (10.4 L) dry fill
items.interval: At purchase. The schedule only calls for ATF changes when towing (60,000 mi), but GXOR says many owners change it anyway.
items.note: A drain-and-fill swaps only about a quarter of the fluid, so do it two or three times. GXOR lists a pan gasket (35168-60010), strainer (35330-60050), strainer O-ring (90301-31014) and drain/fill plug gaskets (35178-30010, two required) if you drop the pan.

items.spec: Hypoid gear oil API GL-5, SAE 75W-90 · 1.5 US qt (1.4 L)
items.interval: At purchase, then every 30,000 mi if you tow (2008 schedule)
items.note: Fill until oil reaches within 5 mm of the bottom edge of the filler hole.

items.spec: Hypoid gear oil API GL-5: SAE 90 above 0 °F, SAE 80W or 80W-90 below · front 1.48 US qt (1.40 L), rear 3.22 US qt (3.05 L)
items.interval: At purchase, then every 15,000 mi if you tow (2008 schedule)
items.note: Rear is the 8 in axle GXOR calls weak. Check the magnetic plug for metal.

parts.name: Front diff drain plug with copper gasket, GX 470/460
Front diff drain plug gasket, GX 470/460

items.note: GXOR says the early support can fail catastrophically and take the oil pan with it. Some 2005s have the updated part from the factory.

items.spec: ATF Dexron II or III · 1.0 US qt (1.0 L) total
items.interval: Check level and leaks at purchase
items.note: Leaks from hoses and the pump can drip onto the rack and look like a rack leak.

items.spec: SAE J1703 or FMVSS No. 116 DOT 3
items.interval: At purchase, then every 30,000 mi (2008 schedule)

items.spec: Lithium-base chassis grease NLGI No. 2 for the spiders and slide yoke
items.interval: Grease at purchase. Grease after water crossings.
items.note: The factory chassis checklist also calls for repacking the front wheel bearings and the drive-shaft bushing grease. Wipe mud off the fittings before you pump in grease.

parts.name: Red-i hi-temp and moly grease kit (6 tubes)

items.spec: Air springs, compressor and height sensor
items.note: Check that the truck holds height overnight and listen for the compressor running often. GXOR says the bags will eventually fail, and the usual fix is a coil conversion.
